intended_object: A transport isomorphism. It identifies the convolution group of R-algebra maps from the coordinate Hopf algebra of SLₙ into `Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra R H B` with the matrix group `SL(n, B)`. The library's counit algebra is just B with an extra H-algebra structure, used to model tangent vectors. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the GL analogue `GeneralLinear.counitPointsMulEquiv`.
explanation:
The definition composes two library isomorphisms. The first is `Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra.pointsMulEquiv`: points valued in the counit algebra are the same as B-points, since an R-algebra map out of H does not see the extra H-algebra structure. The second is `SpecialLinear.pointsMulEquiv`, the canonical identification of the B-points of the SLₙ coordinate Hopf algebra with `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin n) B`.

Mathematically this is only the canonical identification SLₙ(B) ≅ Hom_R(O(SLₙ), B), restated for one particular wrapper of B (`CounitAlgebra`). That wrapper is an implementation device of the library's tangent-space and adjoint-action machinery. The module documentation says so: it exists "so that a computation of the adjoint action stated for counit-algebra-valued points can be read off the ordinary functor of points". It is a bookkeeping transport between two encodings of the same group, not a new mathematical object.

The construction is correct for what it does: the composite is a multiplicative equivalence onto SL(n, B), and it is stated for any commutative ring R, any commutative R-algebra B and any n. So the only point against it as a "faithful formalization" is that it formalizes no standard object of its own.
